title: Return Values and Returning Results
learningObjectives: Explain return values and returning results.
Identify the function's role, inputs and control flow.
Trace calls, local state and returned results.
Recognize common design or safety mistakes.
Write and test a reusable function for a practical task.

understand.concept: A non-void function returns a value compatible with its declared return type. return exits the function immediately. A return value is delivered to the caller, not automatically printed.
understand.whyItMatters: Returning results keeps calculations reusable and lets the caller decide whether to print, store, compare or combine the result.
understand.explain: Every reachable path in a non-void function must return a valid result. Avoid returning references or pointers to local variables whose lifetime ends when the function returns. Separate computation from display when possible.

examples.title: Return a running sum
examples.code: int sumTo(int n){int total=0;for(int i=1;i<=n;++i)total+=i;return total;}\n// sumTo(4) -> 10
examples.explanation: The computed total is passed back to the caller.

examples.title: Return a Boolean
examples.code: bool isPositive(int n){return n>0;}\n// isPositive(-2) is false
examples.explanation: A Boolean return can be used directly in a condition.

examples.title: Early return
examples.explanation: The negative case exits early. Note that negating the minimum int is an overflow edge case.

examples.title: Calculate then print
examples.code: double circleArea(double r){return 3.14159*r*r;}\n// caller prints circleArea(2.0)
examples.explanation: The helper does not force a particular display format.

examples.title: Use result twice
examples.code: int larger(int a,int b){return a>b?a:b;}\nint x=larger(4,9);bool ok=larger(4,9)==9;
examples.explanation: One result can be stored or used in an expression.

practise.guidedTask: Walk through all five Return Values and Returning Results examples. Annotate the signature, call arguments, local state, control flow, return behavior and side effects.
practise.independentTask: Implement functions that return the maximum of two numbers, whether a number is even, and a calculated total. Test their return values without placing output inside each helper.
hints: Start with the function signature and intended contract.
Trace each call with a small input.
Separate calculation from output when appropriate.
Test normal, boundary and invalid cases.
Check lifetimes, side effects and termination.
